thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [INCIDENT] High p95 routing oscillation detected in smart-routing policy 'latency-slo-v2' — repeated reroutes between us-east-1 <-> eu-west-1. Auto-fallback count: 14. Pager: oncall-sre. Link: https://redwood/incident/INC-2026-319

maria: acknowledging, looking. p95 for /v1/generate is bouncing 300ms -> 1200ms and routing is flipping every 30-90s.

jon: I'm on it, grabbing request traces and route decisions. putting a hold on any deploys in routing svc.

oncall-sre: oncall here — taking traffic out of 'latency-slo-v2' auto-policy and setting a static primary to us-east-1 to stop the flip. ETA ~2m.

lee: quick observation from traces: fallbacks are picking the 'm-medium-quant' variant in eu-west which has higher p95 under current kernel; policy treats region latency first but doesn't enforce model-variant compatibility. that mismatch could explain the loop.

maria: do we have an initial customer impact list? Dedicated tenants or hosted users?

oncall-sre: early estimate: 3 Dedicated tenants with heavy real-time prompts in eu-west showing 20-40% p95 spikes and increased tail latency errors; several hosted customers show degraded long-response experiences. no 5xx mass increase yet, mostly timeouts on long-context calls. DMing CS now.

jon: disabling auto-fallback and freezing routing for that policy to stop oscillation:
```
# disable auto-fallback and freeze routing for policy latency-slo-v2
redwoodctl routing update --policy latency-slo-v2 --auto-fallback false --freeze true
```

oncall-sre: ran the command, API returned 200. Confirmed no further reroutes in last 30s. p95 back down to ~260ms and holding.

sam: can we revert the recent policy tweak? change landed ~02:12 UTC that widened region priority list.

maria: tagging who made the change — @elaine any context?

elaine: that was me — I expanded region preference to include eu-west to save costs for low-latency traffic. I didn't include a model-variant compatibility filter when I added the region. starting rollback now.

elaine: rollback command:
```
redwoodctl policy rollback --policy latency-slo-v2 --to-revision 42
```

jon: also recommend increasing p95 evaluation window to smooth transient spikes (1m -> 5m) so we don't flip on short blips:
```
redwoodctl routing update --policy latency-slo-v2 --p95-window 300
```

oncall-sre: applied rollback and p95-window change. monitoring metrics. no reroutes observed for 3m.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident updated — mitigations applied. Severity set to Sev2 -> monitoring. Auto-pager suppressed.

maria: scheduled customer status note in draft for affected tenants, will include timeline of events, mitigations, and next steps. @sam can you own the RCA?

sam: taking RCA. initial notes: root cause is policy config gap — region added without enforcing compatible model-variants; auto-fallback selected slower variant in eu-west which increased p95, triggering routing decision loop. immediate mitigations: freeze policy, rollback change, increase debounce window. follow-ups: add CI guard for variant compatibility in policy changes, add metric/alert for rapid reroute counts, cap reroute rate.

lee: +1 on a metric to count 'fallback-to-slower-variant' events so we can alert before an oscillation. Also propose a safety net: limit reroutes to 1 per 10m per route.

jon: i'll open a quick PR to add reroute rate-limiter in routing svc and add a unit test for variant compatibility checks.

oncall-sre: handing off to day SRE at 08:00 UTC. will continue monitoring for 30m then close pager.

maria: I'll finalize affected customer list and post the status update once RCA ticket exists.

sam: RCA ticket created INC-2026-319-RCA -> https://redwood/ops/INC-2026-319-RCA

incident-bot: :lock: Incident transitioned to follow-up (RCA) state and pager closed. If a regression is detected reopen the incident.

maria: thanks everyone — good catch. closing thread after RCA and customer comms are posted.
